title: One Yardstick for Five Robots: Reach Volume by Sampling, the Room a Robot Takes for It, and What the Numbers Do and Do Not Say

questions.question: Why ask every robot the same question?
options: Their reaches are described in different terms and cannot be compared otherwise
questions.explanation: Can you put the tool here, level?

questions.question: How was the volume found?
options: By asking the question at random points and counting the yes answers

questions.question: Which had the largest reach volume?
questions.explanation: A ball, against the SCARA's slab.

questions.question: The Stewart platform used what share of its room?
questions.explanation: Its base and legs are large for a small stroke.

questions.question: Does the largest volume make the best robot?
options: No: volume leaves out speed, payload, stiffness, accuracy and the shape of the work

questions.question: Why is the standard error of use?
options: It says how many points the estimate needs and is the square root of n small
questions.explanation: Sixteen times the points, a quarter of the error.
